sections.h2: Where is the Lake County, Michigan Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Look for Suite 200 at 800 Tenth Street in Baldwin, the county seat. The clerk and the register of deeds share that one office, so every deed for Lake County land goes across the same counter.

  • Monday to Thursday: 8:30 am until 5:00 pm
  • Friday: 8:30 am until 4:00 pm
  • Phone (231) 745-2725, fax (231) 745-8632

Equalization has its own suite in the same address, Suite 230, with a phone at (231) 745-2723. It maintains property descriptions and helps with assessment questions.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Lake County for a property seller?
sections.html:
Lake County is rural, seasonal and low-priced. About 567 square miles of land hold an estimated 13,182 residents (Census, July 2025), which was close to 21 people per square mile in 2020. Wikipedia notes that the Legislature created it in 1840 as Aischum County, and it took the Lake name in 1843 for its many lakes.

  • Typical owner-occupied home value (2020-2024): $133,900
  • Owner-occupied rate: 82.0%
  • Residents 65 and older: 28.6%
  • Mean commute to work: 34.0 minutes
  • Housing units in 2020: 13,315, with 61.9% vacant

A vacancy share that high means many parcels sit empty for long stretches, so an owner selling one may live far from Baldwin. Call the office with the parcel number to learn what it needs before you mail anything.

sections.h2: How do you pay Lake County recording fees?
sections.html:
Bring or mail a check, money order or cash payment to the clerk's office, because recording fees cannot be paid online. The county's web payment page covers copies, vital records and cremation permits, and the register of deeds page carves out recordable land record fees as the exception.

State law sets the amounts. The amounts in MCL 600.2567 are $30 per recorded document however many pages it runs, $1 per copied page, $5 to certify a recording, and a $5 floor on a records search. Statute lets a charter county adopt another schedule, so phone the office to verify the total first.

sections.h2: What will the transfer tax be on a Lake County sale?
sections.html:
Two layers apply in Baldwin as in the rest of Michigan. The county layer is 55 cents per $500 because Lake County has fewer than 2,000,000 residents (MCL 207.504), and the state layer is $3.75 per $500 (MCL 207.525).

What the statutory rates produce on sample Lake County prices
Sale priceCounty taxState taxTotal
$60,000$66$450$516
$133,900$147.40$1,005$1,152.40
$250,000$275$1,875$2,150

The middle price is the Census median for the county, which rounds up to 268 units of $500. Since the seller bears the tax, the instrument has to show the full value, or a valuation affidavit has to go with it, and any exemption has to be written on it.

sections.h2: What gets a deed rejected at the Lake County register of deeds?
sections.html:
The clerk's office sends back non-compliant instruments with a checklist, and the checklist cites the Michigan statute for each problem. Most are fixable before you submit.

  • Original ink signatures, with each name printed or typed below, matching the notary block.
  • A street number or post office address for every grantee.
  • The drafter's name and address.
  • One statement of the recordable event on line one of page one, in black ink, 10-point type or larger, over a 2.5 inch blank top margin (half an inch on the other margins).
  • Paper no smaller than letter size and no longer than legal.
  • At most four sequential digits of any Social Security number.
  • An attached English translation for any foreign-language text.

Other triggers include a survivor deed with no recorded death certificate, an uncertified court order, a trust document that is not recorded as its own instrument, and a missing date in the acknowledgment.

sections.h2: Where do Lake County owners find assessment forms and parcel data?
sections.html:
The Equalization Department posts them, and it is the first stop for questions that are not about recording. The department runs annual sales and appraisal studies on every class of real property, and it uses them to equalize values across the county's 15 local units of government. State law (MCL 211.34) frames that work around an assessment level of 50% of true cash value.

Its page links to the state forms an owner is most likely to need: the principal residence exemption and homestead form, a request to rescind a PRE, the disabled veterans exemption, and the property transfer affidavit. It also links the Michigan Treasury property tax estimator, which lets you compare millage rates across local units. A seller can use that tool to show a buyer what the tax on the parcel is likely to look like.

Annual apportionment and equalization reports for Lake County are posted on the same page, with years back to 2015 for apportionment, so a buyer or heir can see how the county's values were adjusted from year to year. Equalization also keeps a map of subdivisions for all 83 Michigan counties, and its advice for using that tool is to type only the first two letters of the subdivision name.

sections.h2: Does Lake County offer a land records fraud alert?
sections.html:
Yes. The register of deeds describes itself as the beta test site for a fraud alert program that notifies subscribers when land record activity matches their name. Mail your name, email, phone number, mailing address and parcel ID (if known) to Lake County Register of Deeds, Attn: Fraud Alert, 800 10th Street, Suite 200, Baldwin, Michigan 49304.

An owner who lives elsewhere and holds a cabin or vacant land can use that alert as an early warning that someone has recorded a document against the parcel. The same page links to online land record searches, which you can use to review a parcel's recorded deeds before a sale.

sections.h2: What should a Lake County seller settle before recording?
sections.html:
Deal with taxes first. A deed that carries warranty covenants will not record in Lake County without the county treasurer's certificate under MCL 211.135, which speaks to liens and the last five years of tax. Request it from the Lake County treasurer well ahead of closing.

Equalization covers the 15 local units in the county and about 27,000 real property parcels, with permanent parcel numbers in use since 1987, so keep the number handy when you phone. After closing, the buyer has 45 days to report the transfer to the local assessing office (MCL 211.27a), and next year's taxable value is reset. Whether the buyer finances or pays cash, the steps in this guide are the same.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee at the Lake County register of deeds?
faqs.a: The base fee is $30 for each recorded document, and a discharge or assignment that covers extra instruments costs $3 more per instrument. Take payment to the clerk's office as a check, money order or cash, since the online payment page excludes recording fees.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Lake County register of deeds?
faqs.a: Monday through Thursday it runs 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, and on Friday it closes at 4:00 pm. Go to Suite 200, 800 Tenth Street, Baldwin, or call (231) 745-2725.

faqs.q: Who owes Lake County real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller. Together the two rates are $4.30 per $500 of value, and a deed gets no exemption unless it says so on its face.

faqs.q: Why would the Lake County register of deeds return my deed?
faqs.a: Usually for a formatting or signature problem: no original signatures, no drafter name and address, a missing grantee address, the wrong margins or paper size, or no statement of total value. The office sends back a checklist of the reasons with the instrument.

faqs.q: Can I search Lake County land records online?
faqs.a: Yes. The register's page links to online land records and describes a fraud alert program you join by mail with your details and parcel ID.
